# Results — Study 890 (Sector Risk-Parity)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: cap-weight
concentrates the S&P 500 into a few mega-cap sectors, so **equal-RISK-weighting** the GICS
sectors (inverse-vol, or full equal-risk-contribution) should diversify within equities —
lifting the **excess-of-cash Sharpe** and cutting the drawdown versus cap-weight SPY, net of
quarterly rebalancing costs. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped — the sample is sliced as-of 2026-06-30 so it never creeps).
Fingerprint `5e98273e423e` (eleven-sector price panel; the nine-sector panel is
`2afe10148f92`).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes (`auto_adjust=True`, **total-return**) for the 11 SPDR Select-Sector ETFs + **SPY** (cap-weight benchmark) + **BIL** (cash / risk-free leg), cached under this study's own `_cache/` as parquet |
| Sectors | **XLB XLE XLF XLI XLK XLP XLU XLV XLY** (from 1998-12) + **XLRE** (2015-10) + **XLC** (2018-06) |
| Panels | **Eleven-sector** headline: joint window **2018-06-19 → 2026-06-30** (bounded by XLC's inception — short, tech-bull-dominated). **Nine-sector** long history: **2007-05-30 → 2026-06-30** (bounded by BIL's inception, reaches back through 2008) |
| Weights | **inverse-vol** (risk parity) and full **equal-risk-contribution** (ERC, cyclical coordinate descent), long-only, from a trailing **63-day** covariance **known at the close of the day before each rebalance** (one documented lag, zero look-ahead) |
| Rebalance / costs | **quarterly**, held with realistic daily weight drift; a **3 bps one-way** cost is charged on the turnover (Σ\|Δweight\|) at each rebalance |
| Benchmark | **cap-weight SPY** total return; every Sharpe is **excess of BIL** (both legs minus cash) |
| Statistics | annualised excess-of-cash Sharpe, max drawdown, calendar-year table; a **paired circular-block-bootstrap** 95% CI on the *Sharpe difference* (RP − SPY); a Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the mean daily excess-return difference; an era cut; a levered-to-SPY-vol timer; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Short history — named on the Signal axis.** The *joint eleven-sector* window only starts at
XLC's **2018-06** inception, so the headline panel is ~8 years and dominated by one regime (the
tech / AI bull). The nine-sector panel (2007-) is the fairer, longer read and is where the
robustness cut lives.

## The headline race — risk-parity vs cap-weight SPY (excess of cash, net of 3 bps)

| panel | book | Sharpe | ann. | vol | max DD | Sharpe diff vs SPY | 95% CI | NW *t* (ret diff) |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **11-sector (2018-)** | inverse-vol | **0.572** | +12.73% | 17.74% | −34.7% | **−0.095** | [−0.302, +0.132] | −1.50 |
| | ERC | 0.583 | +13.11% | 18.08% | −35.6% | −0.084 | [−0.325, +0.185] | −1.11 |
| | *cap-weight SPY* | *0.667* | *+15.67%* | *19.62%* | *−33.7%* | — | — | — |
| **9-sector (2007-)** | inverse-vol | **0.555** | +11.16% | 17.76% | **−49.6%** | **+0.002** | [−0.099, +0.110] | −1.12 |
| | ERC | 0.517 | +10.89% | 18.57% | −51.2% | −0.036 | [−0.149, +0.084] | −1.23 |
| | *cap-weight SPY* | *0.553* | *+12.29%* | *19.88%* | *−55.2%* | — | — | — |

The promised **Sharpe improvement is not there.** On the fair long (nine-sector) panel the
inverse-vol book **ties** SPY (diff **+0.002**, bootstrap 95% CI **[−0.099, +0.110]** straddles
zero, NW *t* = −1.12); on the short eleven-sector panel it *loses* (−0.095), because
under-weighting the crowded tech sector cost return over the AI bull. Full ERC tells the same
story. What **is** real is the **risk reduction**: inverse-vol cut annualised volatility to
17.8% (SPY 19.9%) and — over the long panel — max drawdown to **−49.6%** vs SPY's **−55.2%**.
Diversification of *risk*, yes; risk-adjusted *return*, no.

## Era cut — the "advantage" flips sign with the regime

Nine-sector inverse-vol, excess-of-cash Sharpe, split at 2016:

| era | RP Sharpe | SPY Sharpe | diff | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2007-2015 (crisis-heavy) | 0.414 | 0.349 | **+0.064** | 2,079 |
| 2016-2026 (tech / AI bull) | 0.695 | 0.759 | **−0.064** | 2,637 |

A genuine risk-adjusted edge should hold across sub-eras; this one **swaps sign** — risk-parity
won the crisis-heavy first half and lost the tech-led second half, and the two cancel to ~zero
over the full sample. That is the fingerprint of diversification, not alpha.

## Calendar-year total return — inverse-vol (9-sector) vs SPY (pp difference)

Risk-parity wins **7 / 20** years, and the wins cluster in the bad ones: it beat SPY by
**+4.6 pp in 2008** and **+13.3 pp in 2022** (the two genuine bear years), but lagged by
**−14.6 pp in 2023** and **−10.6 pp in 2024** (the AI melt-up, when tech mega-caps — exactly
what risk-parity under-weights — powered the index). The book trims both tails: smaller
crashes, smaller melt-ups.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

* **Costs are trivial.** Quarterly rebalancing turns over ~48%/yr; at 3 bps one-way that is
  **1.4 bps/yr** of drag. The Select-Sector ETFs are among the most liquid instruments on
  Earth — costs are *not* the killer here.
* **Unlevered, you simply earn less.** The nine-sector inverse-vol book returns **+11.16%/yr**
  vs SPY's **+12.29%** — you pay ~1.1 pp/yr of return for the smoother ride and milder drawdown.
* **Levering to SPY's vol reproduces SPY.** Because RP's vol (17.8%) is only slightly below
  SPY's (19.9%), it takes just **1.12×** leverage to match — and the levered book lands at
  Sharpe **0.552** vs SPY **0.553**, ann **+10.97%** vs **+10.99%** (financing drag 7.2 bps/yr,
  levered max DD −54.2%). No free lunch: with no Sharpe edge to amplify, leverage just walks you
  back onto the benchmark.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

A deterministic seeded world where every asset has the SAME Sharpe but a DIFFERENT volatility,
and the cap-weight benchmark piles risk onto the highest-vol names (∝ vol²). No network.

| world | inverse-vol Sharpe advantage over cap-weight |
|---|--:|
| null (`vol_spread = 0`, equal vols), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.0031** (sd 0.0214), **\|adv\| > 0.10 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted (`vol_spread = 0.02`, seed 890) | **+0.136** (RP Sharpe 1.32 vs cap-weight 1.18) |

When vols are dispersed, inverse-vol risk-weighting genuinely out-Sharpes the concentrated
cap-weight benchmark; when all vols are equal it ties (mechanically). So the detector recovers a
*planted* diversification advantage cleanly and never fires on the null — the flat real-tape
result is a true finding, not a broken engine. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never
cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** The claim has two halves and they split. The **drawdown / volatility
  diversification is real and robust**: over 2007–2026 inverse-vol cut vol to 17.8% (SPY 19.9%)
  and max drawdown to −49.6% (SPY −55.2%), beating SPY by +4.6 pp in 2008 and +13.3 pp in 2022.
  But the **excess-of-cash Sharpe advantage does not clear the bar**: it is **+0.002** on the
  long panel (bootstrap 95% CI [−0.099, +0.110] straddles zero, NW *t* = −1.12), **−0.095** on
  the 2018– panel, and it *flips sign* across eras (+0.064 → −0.064). Real risk reduction, no
  risk-adjusted edge. *Short history on the eleven-sector panel (XLC from 2018-06) named above.*
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Costs are negligible (1.4 bps/yr) and capacity is effectively
  unlimited, but there is no Sharpe edge to harvest: unlevered you earn *less* than SPY
  (+11.16% vs +12.29%) for the smoother ride, and levering back to SPY's vol just reproduces SPY
  (Sharpe 0.552 vs 0.553). The promised risk-adjusted pickup is a mirage; what remains is a
  lower-beta equity book, not a bankable edge.
